page.layout: One page of text, verse emblems with headings; running head at top; page number top left; manuscript annotations in Greek and Latin in the left margin and handwritten Greek at lower left and foot (not printed, not transcribed); faint notes in right margin are show-through.

main_text.head: Falsa moneta. Principum corruptores.
main_text.p: Effigiem falso qui regis adulterat ære, Supplicio dignum quis neget esse graui? Regis at ingenium foedat qui moribus atris, Dic mihi, supplicio quo feriendus erit? Edicant Minos, Rhadamantus & Æacus ipsi. Namque potest hominum dicere nemo satis.
main_text.head: Rosa genista insita. Radicari in Christo.
main_text.p: Flava genista rosam flauentem reddere fertur, Altera si radix hæret in alterius: Cum Christo fueris si radicatus, eidem Conformem faciet te sociatus amor.
main_text.head: Tumor animi deprimitur cognitione Dei & sui.
main_text.p: Infestos quæ discutiant à corpore flatus, Multa legunt Medicæ femina nota manus. At tumidi flatus animi qui tundere possis, Clara Dei monstrat notio, clara mei.
main_text.head: Nepenthes herba, ex Homero. Christianorum bona conscientia.
main_text.p: A Nilo quorsum petitur cantata poetis Herba, dolore leuans pectora presca graui? Nepenthes verum mens est sibi conscia recti: Amplectens Christum non moriente fide.
main_text.head: Palumbes. Maligni rebus aliorum latis dolentes.
main_text.p: Dum reliquæ mulcent volucres concentibus auras, Vere, palumbus iners, adueniente, gemit. O, hominum nullis natura probanda palumbi! Quo gaudent reliqui namque dolere, nefas.

page.notes: Printed Greek heading words in the margin are handwritten annotations and were not transcribed. Doubtful readings: "presca" in line 2 of the Nepenthes stanza, "possis" and "mei" in the Tumor stanza; "Tole-" at the foot is a catchword-like hyphenated fragment. Left margin contains manuscript Greek annotations, not printed text.
